p.seg: Having lost dozens of cities,
and the kingdom's troubles remain unresolved,
it is the king who abandons them,
not employs them.
Now, Qín's strength
is such that it has no equal under Heaven,
and Wèi's weakness is extreme.
Yet the king uses this to pledge allegiance to Qín,
and the king can only die but cannot abandon it;
this is a double fault.
Now, if the king can employ my plan,
ceding land will not be enough to harm the kingdom,
humbling yourself will not be enough to cause personal suffering,
and troubles will be resolved and resentment repaid."
"Within Qín's four borders,
from the law enforcers down to the long-haul drivers,
they all invariably say:
'Is it with Lào Ǎi?
Is it with Lǚ Bùwéi?'
Even down to those below the gates of the village,
and those above in the halls of the court,
it is still the same.
Now, the king cedes land to bribe Qín,
thinking it is Lào Ǎi's merit;
humbles himself to honor Qín,
to rely on Lào Ǎi.
The king uses the kingdom to support Lào Ǎi,
Because Lào Ǎi was victorious.
The king is using the state to support the Lào clan,
The Empress Dowager's kindness towards the king,
is deep in his bones,
the king's relationships are the highest in the land.
Qín and Wèi, they interact with each other a hundred times,
and deceive each other a hundred times.
Now, because the Lào clan is good to Qín, his relationships are the highest in the land,
who in the world would not abandon the Lǚ clan and follow the Lào clan?
The world will surely unite against the Lǚ clan and follow the Lào clan,
then the king's resentment will be avenged."
The King of Qín sent a man to tell the Lord of Ānlíng
The King of Qín sent a man to tell the Lord of Ānlíng, saying:
"I want to exchange five hundred *lǐ* of land for Ānlíng,
will the Lord of Ānlíng agree to my request?"
The Lord of Ānlíng said: "Your Majesty shows kindness,
exchanging a large one for a small one,
that is very good.
However, I received this land from my predecessors,
and I wish to guard it to the end,
I dare not exchange it."
The King of Qín was displeased.
Therefore, the Lord of Ānlíng sent Táng Qiě as an envoy to Qín.
The King of Qín said to Táng Qiě:
"I wanted to exchange five hundred *lǐ* of land for Ānlíng,
but the Lord of Ānlíng would not listen to me,
why is that?
Qiě Qín miè Hán wáng Wèi,
and you were able to survive with your fifty li of land,
it was because I considered you a man of integrity,
and therefore did not act against your wishes.
Now I offer you ten times that land,
asking to enlarge your territory,
yet you oppose me,
do you take me lightly?"
Táng Qiě replied, "No,
it is not like that.
The Lord of Ānlíng received this land from his ancestors and guards it.
Even for a thousand li, he would not dare exchange it,
how much less for just five hundred li?"
The King of Qin angrily flared up,
and said to Táng Qiě:
"Have you ever heard of the wrath of the Son of Heaven?"
Táng Qiě replied,
"Your subject has never heard of it."
The King of Qin said:
"The wrath of the Son of Heaven
results in a million corpses lying down
and blood flowing for a thousand li."
Táng Qiě said:
"Has Your Majesty ever heard of the wrath of a common man?"
The King of Qin said:
"The wrath of a common man
is merely taking off his hat and walking barefoot,
smashing his head on the ground."
Táng Qiě 唐且 said:
"This is the anger of a common man,
not the anger of a scholar.
a comet struck the moon;
when Niè Zhèng 聶政 assassinated Hán Kuí 韓傀,
a white rainbow pierced the sun;
when Yào Lí 要離 assassinated Qìng Jì 慶忌,
a falcon struck down in the palace hall.
These three men,
were all scholars from common backgrounds.
When their anger was held back and not yet released,
ominous signs descended from the heavens.
Add me to them, and there will be four.
If a scholar must be angry,
two corpses will lie prostrate,
blood will flow five paces,
and the world will be clothed in white mourning.
Today is that day!"
He drew his sword and stood up.
The Qín 秦 king's countenance changed,
he knelt and apologized, saying:
"Please sit, sir. Why go to such lengths?
I understand.
The states of Hán 韓 and Wèi 魏 have been destroyed,
yet Ānlíng 安陵 has survived with fifty *lǐ* 里 of land,
solely because you are here, sir."
The Three Jìn 晉 had already defeated the Zhì 智 clan.
Sān Jìn had already defeated the Zhì clan and
were about to divide their territory.
Duàn Guī said to the King of Hán:
"When dividing the territory, you must take Chénggāo."
The King of Hán said: "Chénggāo
is a rocky, barren place;
I have no use for it."
Duàn Guī said:
"Not so.
I have heard that the power to influence events a thousand *lǐ* away
depends on the advantage of a territory
only one *lǐ* thick.
That ten thousand men
can defeat an entire army
is due to unexpected circumstances.
If Your Majesty takes my advice,
then Hán will certainly take Zhèng."
The king said, "Good."
He indeed took Chénggāo.
The taking of Zhèng by Hán
indeed began from Chénggāo.
Dàchéng Wǔ came from Zhào
Dàchéng Wǔ came from Zhào and
said to Shēn Bùhài in Hán:
"You use Hán to make me important in Zhào,
I will use Zhào to make you important in Hán.
In this way, you will have two Hàn,
And I have two Zhao."

Wei's siege of Handan,
Shēn Bùhài began to ally with the King of Han,
but he did not know what the king desired,
fearing that if he spoke, he might not hit the king's intentions.
The king asked Shēnzi, saying:
"Who should I side with to be acceptable?"
He replied:
"This is the key to safety and danger,
a major affair of the state.
I beg to think deeply and ponder it carefully."
Then he secretly said to Zhào Zhuō and Hán Cháo:
"You are all skilled debaters of the state,
for those who are ministers,
their words must be followed,
and they should only do their utmost to be loyal."
The two men each presented their proposals to the king regarding the matter.
Shēnzi subtly observed what pleased the king and spoke to the king accordingly,
and the king was greatly pleased.
Shēnzi requested an official position for his cousin.
Shēnzi requested an official position for his cousin,
but Marquis Zhāo did not grant it.
Shēnzi showed a look of resentment.
Marquis Zhāo said:
"This is not what it means to learn from you.
Are you listening to the audience that you hold,
and abandoning your own principles?
Are you also losing your ability to practice your methods,
and abandoning the audience that you hold?
You once taught me to follow meritorious service
and regard rank.
Now there is a request,
what should I listen to?"
Shēn Zǐ then withdrew and requested punishment,
saying:
"You are truly the right person!"
Sū Qín advocating alliance on behalf of Chǔ, persuading the King of Hán
Sū Qín advocating alliance on behalf of Chǔ, persuaded the King of Hán, saying:
"To the north, Hán has the defenses of Gǒng, Luò, and Chénggāo;
to the west, it has the passes of Yíyáng and Chángbǎn;
to the east, it has Wǎn, Rǎng, and the Wěi River;
to the south, it has Xíngshān Mountain;
its territory is a thousand *lǐ* in extent;
it has hundreds of thousands of armored soldiers.
The strongest bows and most powerful crossbows in the world
all come from Hán.
Xī Zǐ, Shàofǔ Shílì, and Jù Lái
can all shoot beyond six hundred paces.
The soldiers of Hán, standing on tiptoe and shooting,
can fire hundreds of arrows without stopping,
the far ones reaching the chest,
the near ones covering the heart.
The swords and halberds of the Hàn soldiers
all come from Míng Mountain, Táng Xī, Mò Yáng, and Hé Bó Bó.
Dèng Shī, Wǎn Féng, Lóng Yuān, and Dà Ā,
all on land can cut through horses and cattle,
and on water can strike swans and geese;
when facing enemies, they immediately cut through the tough defenses.
Armor, shields, felt blankets, helmets, iron curtains,
leather thimbles, and ǒu ruì (types of armor),
all are completely equipped.
With the bravery of the Hàn soldiers,
wearing strong armor,
holding powerful crossbows,
carrying sharp swords,
one man can match a hundred,
it is an understatement to say.
Now, with Hàn's strength
and Your Majesty's wisdom,
you actually want to face west and serve Qín,
call yourselves an eastern vassal,
build an imperial palace,
receive hats and belts,
conduct seasonal sacrifices,
cross your arms and submit to them.
To shame the state altars and be laughed at by the world,
nothing surpasses this.
Therefore, I hope that Your Majesty will carefully consider this.
If Your Majesty serves Qín,
Qín will certainly demand Yíyáng and Chénggāo.
If you comply with this now,
next year they will again seek to seize more land.
If you give it to them,
you will have no land to give;
if you do not give it to them,
then you will abandon your previous efforts and suffer even greater misfortune.
Moreover, the land of Your Majesty is finite,
but the demands of Qin are endless.
To use finite land
to satisfy endless demands,
this is what is meant by inviting resentment and buying trouble,
and your land is already being diminished without fighting.
I have heard a vulgar saying:
'Better to be the mouth of a chicken,
than the rear of an ox.'
Now, for Your Majesty to face west, bind your arms, and serve Qin,
how is that different from being the rear of an ox?
With Your Majesty's wisdom,
wielding the strong armies of Hàn,
to have the name of the rear of an ox,
I am ashamed for Your Majesty."
The King of Hàn angrily changed his expression,
rolled up his sleeves and gripped his sword,
looked up to the sky and sighed deeply, saying:
"Even if I die,
I will never serve Qin.
Now, my lord has informed me of the teachings of the King of Chǔ,
I will respectfully offer up the altars of soil and grain and follow them."
Zhāng Yí, on behalf of Qín, advocated the policy of horizontal alliance to the King of Hán.
Zhāng Yí wèi Qín lián héng shuō Hán Wáng yuē:
"The land of Hán is perilous,
situated in the mountains.
The grains produced
are mostly beans rather than wheat.
The food of the people
is mostly bean rice and vegetable soup.
If there is a single year of crop failure,
the people will not even have dregs to satisfy their hunger.
The territory is less than nine hundred *lǐ*,
insufficient to provide food for two years.
Estimating Your Majesty's soldiers,
the total number is no more than three hundred thousand,
and servants and laborers are included within that number.
If you deduct those guarding borders, watchtowers, barriers, and fortifications,
the visible soldiers are no more than two hundred thousand.
Qín has over a million armored soldiers,
a thousand chariots,
ten thousand horses,
and fierce warriors
who leap and bound, with their hair unbound,
piercing their cheeks and brandishing spears,
in numbers too great to count.
The excellence of Qín's horses,
the multitude of its barbarian soldiers,
Stumbling forward and tripping backward,
those whose horses' hooves cover only three xún,
are too numerous to count.
The soldiers of Shāndōng,
wearing armor and helmets to engage in battle,
the men of Qín discarded their armor and bared themselves to rush at the enemy,
in their left hand holding a severed head,
and in their right arm carrying a captured prisoner.
The relationship between the soldiers of Qín and the soldiers of Shāndōng,
is like that of Mèng Bēn and a coward;
to press down with great force,
is like Wū Huò with a baby.
If Mèng Bēn and Wū Huò's soldiers,
are used to attack weak, unsubmissive states,
it is no different from dropping a thousand-jūn weight,
onto a bird's egg,
there will certainly be no survival.
The lords do not consider the weakness of their soldiers,
or the scarcity of their food supplies,
but listen to the sweet words and fine rhetoric of others,
and collude to embellish each other,
all saying:
'If you listen to my plan, you can become a powerful hegemon over the world.'
To disregard the long-term interests of the state,
and listen to fleeting arguments,
those who mislead the ruler,
there is nothing that exceeds this.
If Your Majesty does not serve Qín,
Qín will send down its armored troops to seize Yíyáng,
cutting off the upper territories of Hán;
and if they take Chénggāo and Yíyáng to the east,
then the palace of Hóngtái,
and the Sānglín gardens,
will no longer be yours.
If Chenggao is blocked,
and the upper lands cut off,
then Your Majesty's kingdom will be divided.
Serving Qin first brings peace,
not serving Qin brings danger.
To create disaster and seek fortune,
to have shallow plans and deep resentment,
to go against Qin and follow Chu,
even if you wish not to perish,
it is unattainable.
Therefore, my plan for Your Majesty
is that nothing is better than serving Qin.
What Qin desires most
is nothing more than weakening Chu,
and none can weaken Chu better than Han.
It's not that Han is stronger than Chu,
but the geography makes it so.
Now, if Your Majesty faces west and serves Qin to attack Chu,
acting as a vanguard,
the King of Qin will surely be pleased.
Attacking Chu and annexing its land privately,
turning disaster into pleasing Qin,

"It would be better for Your Majesty to support Hán Péng,

Chén Zhěn said to the King of Qín:
"The state's terrain is not convenient for swift action, therefore you yield territory;
your relations are not close, therefore you cede land.
Now you have ceded land, but your relations are not closer;
you have hurried, but the military actions do not stop.
I fear that the states east of the mountains (Shāndōng) will have nothing left to yield or cede to serve Your Majesty.
Moreover, Your Majesty sought a hundred *jin* of gold from the Three Rivers region (Sānchuān) and could not obtain it,
but sought a thousand *jin* of gold from Hán,
and it was supplied in a single day.
Now Your Majesty attacks Hán; this
severs superior relationships and strengthens your private treasury.
I privately believe that it is not wise for Your Majesty to take this course."

"Now that the five states have disbanded,
they will surely attack Shìqiū
to recoup their military expenses.
If you finance me,
I will ask to stop the world from attacking Shìqiū on your behalf."
Lord Shìqiū said:
"Good."
Thereupon he sent him.

"Your Majesty made a pact with the five states and attacked Qín to the west.
If you cannot harm Qin,
the world will then, because of this, belittle you, O King, and value Qin;
therefore, why does Your Majesty not seek diplomatic relations?"
King of Chu said:

Wèi Shùn said:
"The world is weary [of war],
and will surely attack Shìqiū to pay for military expenses.
Your Majesty should order them not to attack Shìqiū.
If the five states value Your Majesty,
they will listen to Your Majesty's words and not attack Shìqiū;
if they do not value Your Majesty,
they will go against Your Majesty's words and attack Shìqiū.
Then Your Majesty's importance will surely be clear."
Therefore, the King of Chǔ sought diplomatic relations, and Shìqiū was preserved.

Zhèng Qiáng loaded eight hundred gold into Qin,

Qin will surely not listen to you.

Zhèng Qiáng said:

it was because of the existence of the Ji Sè family there,
Therefore, it should be spoken of before Chu.
Now I have already ordered the King of Chu to take the *jǐ sè* (a type of zither) and one hundred chariots to reside in Yángdí,
and ordered Zhāo Xiàn to transfer and reside with him.
For over ten days,
he has already become aware.
And the *jǐ sè*,
is Gōngshū's enemy;
and Zhāo Xiàn,
is a person of Gōngshū.
When the King of Qin hears of this,
he will surely suspect Gōngshū of being for Chu."

Zhèng Qiáng drove Zhāng Yí to Qin,

if Qin attacks Western Zhōu,

zé Lóu Huǎn bì bài yǐ.

Qín and Hán fought at Zhuózé,

Gōngzhòng Míng said to the King of Hán:
"Allied states are not to be relied upon.
Now, Qín's intention is to attack Chǔ.
Your Majesty should use Zhāng Yí to make peace with Qín,
bribe him with a famous city,
and join him in attacking Chǔ.
This is a plan to exchange one for two."
The King of Hán said:
"Good."
He prepared Gōngzhòng's journey
to go west and negotiate with Qín.
The King of Chǔ, hearing of this, was greatly afraid
and summoned Chén Zhěn to inform him.
Chén Zhěn said:
"Qín's desire to attack us has been long-standing.
Now we have acquired one of Hán's famous cities, fully equipped with armor,
if Qín and Hán join forces to head south,
this is what Qín has been praying for in its ancestral temples.
Now that they have obtained it,
the state of Chǔ will certainly be attacked. Your Majesty,
heed my advice,
prepare troops within the four borders of our state, selecting soldiers,
and declare that we are rescuing Hán.
Let war chariots fill the roads;
send trustworthy envoys,
increase the number of their carriages,
and make their gifts substantial,
so that Hán will believe that we are truly coming to their aid.
Even if Hán is unable to listen to us,
Hán will certainly be grateful to Your Majesty,
and will certainly not act like a goose flying in formation to obey Qín.
If Qín and Hán are not in harmony,
even if the troops arrive,
the state of Chǔ will not suffer a major affliction.
If Hán is able to heed our advice and sever its alliance with Qín,
Qín will certainly be greatly angered,
and harbor deep resentment towards Hán.
If Hán receives Chǔ's assistance,
it will certainly take Qín lightly.
Taking Qín lightly,
its response to Qín will certainly not be respectful.
In this way, we can ensnare the armies of Qín and Hán,
and avert disaster for the state of Chǔ."
The King of Chu was greatly pleased,
and thus he alerted the army within his four borders and selected soldiers,
proclaiming he would rescue Han.
He dispatched trusted ministers,
increased their carriages,
and enriched their gifts.
He said to the King of Han:
"Although our humble state is small,
we have already mobilized all of it.
We wish that your great country would then freely vent its anger on Qin,
and our humble state will use Chu to die for Han."

Qin;

Chu.

and rashly cutting off the enmity with powerful Qin,
will surely be laughed at by the world.

nor have they previously agreed and plotted to attack Qin.

and Chu is therefore raising an army, claiming to rescue Han;
this must be a scheme of Chén Zhěn.
Moreover, you, O King, have already sent a messenger to report to Qin;
"If you do not go now,
it would be deceiving Qin.
To underestimate the calamity of a strong Qin
and trust the advisors of Chu,
Your Majesty will surely regret it."
The King of Han did not listen,
and consequently severed relations with Qin.
Qin was indeed greatly angered,

Chu's rescue did not arrive,

It wasn't that the Han clan's soldiers were weakened,
nor that the people were ignorant.
The army was captured by Qin,
and their wisdom was laughed at by Chu.
They excessively listened to Chén Zhěn,
and lost their strategy because of Hán Míng.
